findings.what: The recovered whole-case containment boundary still omits the public create path.
findings.why: create_case resolves the caller's root before any _scan_case_tree call and never scans the prospective case. A symlinked root is followed and an unrelated nested symlink can remain inside a newly created case, so the public writer can create/write through a case path that inspect_case, resume_case, and decorated writers correctly reject. AC7 says every public resume/read/write path is protected, and the plan-owned tests cover inspect/resume/register/dynamic continuation but not create_case. Add a behavioral create-case root/nested-link test, then scan the unresolved path before resolve or any write.

findings.what: P7 completion does not validate the identities or existence of the outputs that README advertises.
findings.why: The sole P7 identity is gate_b, and _identity_files maps it only to .anomaly/receipts/gate-b.json. findings/findings.json, findings/report.md, findings/unresolved.md, findings/charts, and the charts receipt are absent from resume invalidation. Deleting or modifying a completed report therefore leaves completed_phase=P7; load_snapshot projects Status: complete and links to a missing or stale output. This breaks complete invalidation and truthful README completion in AC4/AC5. Add a consumer test that removes or changes each authoritative P7 output after completion and expects invalidation from P7 plus README demotion, then bind those outputs into the P7 identity/receipt validation.

findings.what: The input-capability boundary remains only shape-aware, not schema-aware, for source and human-decision values.
findings.why: source_requests accepts any values when the required keys are present, while _is_complete_mapping accepts list/tuple decision collections without validating their elements or Gate A's required non-empty selection. Inputs such as approved_ids=[1] or accepted_claim_ids=[None] are classified as complete, enter run_attempts, and are rejected only by the owner after an attempt has been consumed; equivalent malformed source fields do the same. That contradicts the locked schema-aware-input/human-turn repair and boundary-validation standard. Add malformed-value public tests proving no attempt is spent, and make capability derivation perform the complete input schema check (or reject explicitly before execution).

findings.what: No behavioral test proves journalled promotion rollback or interrupted-promotion recovery.
findings.why: The revised AC3 tests demonstrate that an owner failure before promotion cannot leak an earlier source or P7 output, but none exercises a failure/interruption after _apply begins or the new recover_interrupted_promotion path. The acceptance criterion explicitly requires atomic promotion and durable recovery, so this consumer-observable restart contract is owed. Add deterministic failure/restart coverage that observes the live case restored to the last sealed state, the attempt rewound consistently, and a fresh resolution succeeding; do not assert private call order.

findings.what: Installed documentation still resurrects the removed runner and states the wrong resume authority and constant owner.
findings.why: The skill says a durable runner records phases, later tells readers to resume from the last completed event, and at lines 246-247 says MAX_ATTEMPTS lives in workflow.py where 'the runner' enforces it. Current code has no runner, events are explicitly observational, completion comes from state.completed, and MAX_ATTEMPTS is owned by state.py/run_attempts. Incorrect method documentation is a bug and violates AC8's runner/stale-expectation removal. Rewrite these claims to the resolver → owner → run_attempts/state model.

findings.what: run_workflow resolves every snapshot twice even after the invocation entry phase is already known.
findings.why: The first result is used only to initialize entry_phase, yet both resolve_workflow calls run on every later loop iteration. Restrict the preliminary resolution to entry_phase is None, then perform the capability-filtered resolution once; this is a behavior-preserving simplification and removes avoidable computation.
